prompt: A software company wants to cut costs by 15%. The candidate's framework: (1) Employee costs: engineering, sales and support; (2) Office rent; (3) Marketing and events. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 1 and 2 overlap: office rent depends on headcount
options.feedback: Rent rises with headcount, but staff pay and rent are separate cost lines with separate levers.

options.text: Missing: cloud hosting and software subscriptions
options.feedback: Right. For a software company, cloud and tool spend is often one of the largest cost lines after people.

options.text: Bucket 2 doesn't belong: most software staff work remotely
options.feedback: Nothing says staff are remote. Office rent is a real cost that can be cut.

options.text: It's a generic cost list: software costs are better split by product
options.feedback: Splitting by cost type is a valid, complete cut. The flaw is that a large cost line is missing.

explanation: A software cost base is mostly people, cloud infrastructure, third-party tools, marketing and facilities. Infrastructure and tools are missing.

extras.corrected_framework: People; cloud and infrastructure; third-party tools; marketing; facilities
